result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both give exactly one spoken opening with no statistics, preamble or offer to refine. B is a tighter hook: it asks the hygienists themselves whether they have ever overstated their flossing to their own dentist, so the room feels the talk's point before it starts. A's bleeding gumline and mirror are vivid and clinical, but the 'sitting in this chair, with a mirror in my hand' wording leaves it unclear who is in the chair, which weakens the punchline. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers give a single opening, with no statistics and no preamble. A turns the question around neatly: hygienists are asked whether they have ever told their own dentist they floss daily, which leads straight into the talk's theme of why patients say it when it isn't true. B is more vivid, but its 'sitting in this chair, with a mirror in my hand' setup is hard to follow from a podium, and it is less clear who is the patient and who is the clinician.
